## Construction and source map

All new fully qualified names are under `YulangClosure.ProviderNativeContextR57`. The constructor accepts primitive records, including R55's primitive Native/Query/Probe/HIR-shaped records. It never accepts an unexplained semantic Inputs or Context as its input. An `out : Context` appears only in theorem statements constrained by the actual availableContext result equation.

- `ValueEndpoint` preserves every frozen native constructor, including positive/negative Function/Variant/Record/Tuple and tuple arity, constants and raw ValueRow. `EffectEndpoint` preserves BottomPositive, EmptyNegative, Contribution, Allowance, Support, AnnotationMember(view,ordinal) and raw EffectRow.
- `Key Source Term` tags source payloads, state-qualified value/effect row coordinates and full value/effect atom constructors. `Source` retains the original full branded source/declaration/family payload; an actual extraction must use an injective tagged carrier for the heterogeneous native identities. No name/hash/canonical representative substitutes for it. Nat fixtures are finite witnesses, not Arc/pointer identity proofs.
- `Fact.semantic(store,index)` and `Fact.collected(batch,index)` are disjoint, even when both integers coincide. This directly reflects separate `ConstraintStore::facts` and `ConstraintBatch.occurrences`, and the new Rust `ProviderFactOwner`.
- Primitive Bound/Slot/Admission/Emission/Physical records preserve raw owner, polarity, all eight lane constructors, index, original admission index, constructor readback slot/bound and relation. ValueRow/EffectRow retain canonical representatives separately from the raw owner indices. SourceFact retains raw and canonical endpoint pairs separately; no quotient is used to select a physical slot.
- Complete native inventories precede selection: admissions, emissions, both kinds of rows, relations, owner-qualified directed dependency projections, origins/drains, separate fact owners, every view and every resolved operation.

### Summary flags and represented physical slots

VariableBounds also retains `has_int_positive_lower`/`has_unit_positive_lower`; EffectBounds retains bottom/empty summary flags. R47.RowBounds has exactly four physical-vector fields and no flag fields. This Lean construction copies the original exact atom vectors and retains the full Int/Unit/Bottom/Empty native constructors already in those vectors; it never prepends synthetic atoms or changes physical indices. Frozen lib.rs:16360–16382 sets int/unit flags after appending the corresponding atom, and :13900 updates the bottom flag after its append. The Rust projection retains the summary fields, but no separate summary-flag reader or all-history flag/vector invariant is proved here. Claiming such a reader would exceed the existing R47 target.

## Coverage, availability and applications

`provider_inventory_coverage` is an iff between membership in the computed provider list and an actual member position of some owning view satisfying the raw owner/origin/family checks. It assumes no selected singleton table. `complete_owner_traversal` proves no physical slot is silently dropped by a successful Option traversal. `every_physical_owner_slot` and `every_closed_support_member` connect native owner coordinates to the constructed graph.

`SimplePath` records the original visited-endpoint discipline, edge membership and orientation. Its freshness, member and Nodup lemmas prove that any such path has at most the complete edge-inventory length. `all_simple_paths_covered` then proves coverage by the actual walk enumerator at that derived fuel, with no supplied fuel bound or selected-path-uniqueness premise. `available_context_covers_all_simple_paths` transports this into the returned existing Context. This is coverage of the explicit primitive graph, not a theorem about the Rust worklist implementation.

`ancestry` computes a deterministic first dependency witness; entry-row physical probes and the separate entry probe use that same canonical payload. The early idea of empty ancestry on every edge was replaced before any source-qualified completion claim, because it would cover only root-equals-emission cases. No universal root-equality premise was introduced.

`Ready` is a decidable set of primitive owner/inventory checks, the independently defined full enumerator results, original entry coordinates, R55 duplicate-formal guard and native completed-search status. It does not call Authenticated/authenticate. `availableContext` returns None on failed status, missing provenance, unequal full edge inventory, inadequate fuel, competing provider or path candidates. It does not convert a failed search into an authenticated empty list. `available_context_iff` exposes all of these checks rather than hiding them in a whole interpretation assumption; `available_context_uses_r55_fragment` proves its actual internalInputs is the returned R55 fragment.

`context` is the total raw mathematical assembly of the exact existing Context type; the fallible `availableContext` is the owner/search-checked constructor. Generic consumer lemmas specialize the unchanged existing suppression iff and KnownUnmatched rule to that assembled value. The KnownUnmatched application explicitly retains selected-arm, source-operation, full declaration inequality and native providerCandidate premises. Raw mathematical assembly alone establishes none of those reads or availability checks.

The finite fixture constructs all source/Internal and provider/native values, not an old Context fixture. It proves derived graph/Ready/namespace reads, successful availableContext, authenticate=true and actual suppression of the exact member. A separately constructed differing-declaration context proves KnownUnmatched Forward. Another theorem proves observer unavailability with the corresponding Forward; this is a model coexistence witness, not Rust runtime behavior.

Falsifiers proved: equal semantic/batch numeric fact index88 with distinct owners; value/effect rows sharing ordinal4; distinct native effect constructors sharing ordinal7; foreign State rows/dependencies; stale readback; reversed dependency; raw4 versus canonical40; reordered support members; removed candidate edges; an additional matching provider view retained as a second candidate; an additional physical path retained as a second path; insufficient work/fuel, missing provider inventory and failed status. Original order/multiplicity and repeated permission family `[7,7,11]` are retained.

## Exact open source-model seam / first remaining obligation

No Rust→Lean correspondence is claimed. The first remaining source obligation is a field-by-field encoding of the same borrowed `ProviderNativeContextProjection` into these primitive records, with exact heterogeneous Source keys, state/store/batch ownership, Dependency variant→directed-parent projection, origin/drain task/source joins, and complete candidate-search status. In particular, prove that successful Rust `certified_lower_paths` and full provider enumeration correspond to the Lean simple-path/provider candidate tables, and that every Rust allocation/ambiguity/work-limit failure maps to unavailable.

The native search does not persist a traversal trace. No such trace or theorem is invented. The Lean traversal conservatively checks every physical lower slot in its supplied owner graph, while the Rust worklist checks reached slots and also performs per-search ancestry/error checks; a source-correspondence argument must account for this difference. Thus the finite graph theorem is not silently equated to all Rust search executions, and the successful finite fixture is not an extraction theorem for all supported sources. No additional whole-interpretation or FaithfulExtraction premise was introduced to label that gap proved.

After source correspondence, R51 per-call primitive origin/drain/emission cuts, whole publication integration and the original source semantics remain separate open obligations. Original A/B, SourceProblem.InferenceSoundness, principality, termination, full hygiene and production remain OPEN. The registered primary/reviewer owns source qualification and integration; this leaf does not self-certify them.
